I'm moving and gonna be getting a new apartment, it's gonna be sorta a low end luxury apartment for roughly $1k a month. Was wondering what are some good ways to negotiate an apartment cost? I hear it's harder to negotiate at these kinds of places since the complexes feel like they have more leverage. Was wondering what would be a good strategy?

Surely atleast one of you guys out there has read The Art of the Deal
How to negotiate a new apartment

It completely depends on the vacancy rates. Where I live landlords can run waiting lists and there's no shortage of people that will bribe them to get an apartment.

If there's a high vacancy rate where you live, and the landlord can't easily get someone else to rent it if you don't you might have some leverage.

As you go up market there is less negotiating on price since they don't want problem tenants who are shaky about making their rent regularly. If you're not sure you can afford it, they don't want you, so don't act like that. Tell them you like the apartment but want to compare a couple of other places before you decide. Mention some flaw in the unit that they can't easily fix such as old appliances, no fireplace or lack of gym even if you don't care about it. If they have too many open units, they may offer you an upgrade to a better view or larger unit that usually rents for more. If it's early in the month, they may offer no charge for the partial first month. It all depends on supply and demand.

If the unit has been open for a couple months, landlord might be willing to negotiate. Most places, the demand for rentals is so high right now that most landlords will happily pass on tenants looking to negotiate.

Act like you’re shopping around for a specific apt with specific criteria. Ie main room window faces east, bedroom windows facing west, floor plans etc)

Then use that approach to get the leasing agent to tell you how many empty units there are.

If they admit there are a lot of vacancies you should have some leverage. Try using it to negotiate a move in special, lease term special, or ask if they plan on doing any discounted rates after the summer (called the “takeaway”)

However, higher end property managers know full well not to make this mistake and will only show you a few apts claiming theyre almost at full capacity (called “time pressure” or “scarcity rule”) don’t believe it right away. Ask to look at the building directory/map and keep asking questions. Point to different units and models and ask for them to double and triple heck.

They reluctantly admit that there are other units available.

I did this before and my rent price went from $1600 down to $1300/mth. Currently, the price is at $1650.

Unsure what move rates are in your area, but you can also go to some other nearby apts that you’re not looking at seriously and do some recon.

You can also claim that you have an existing lease that might wish to break in order to move closer to work. You could claim that breaking the lease would cost you $x and see if they offer you a deal to cover some of those costs.

Just some initial thoughts. But always 100% if he time dress in business casual and go RIGHT AFER LUNCH - that’s when agents are the happiest/best mood and you can play it off like you need to get back to work. This forces the agent to talk faster and thus you have the advantage if they accidentally make a poor move (ie offer a move in special or free WiFi etc)
